doc: Standing, client-free decisions of the skeleton writer (Spec 48 §3.4). Everything a draft element can be asked that the framework database cannot answer: which text patterns are Site Info, which lines exist only because of the designer's brief, which structural shapes are a column label or a link list. A block named here must exist in the framework database (checked on every load by lib/skeleton-facts.mjs::decisionsProblems). Client-specific choices live in sites/<client>/build/skeleton/decisions.json, written by `skeleton.mjs decide`.

columnLabel.reason: the first text child of a wrapper whose other children are a run of links is the column heading

linkList.reason: a run of two or more bare text links, one above the next, is one list block; the same links side by side are separate links in a row

briefOnlyLines.reason: a coming-soon line exists only because the designer's brief said the thing is not ready; it has no place on a live page
placeholder copy is replaced by real content, never built
a note that the draft's photographs are stand-ins exists only for the design review; the live site uses the client's own photographs

phone.reason: a typed UK phone number standing alone is the Site Info phone

email.reason: a typed email address standing alone is the Site Info email

copyright.reason: a line opening with a copyright mark (the marker business-info's own render uses)

hours.reason: a day name followed by a clock time (9:30, 9am) or "closed"

attribution.reason: a credit line for the agency that built the site

addressLinkPatterns.reason: a link to a maps host is an address link

logoImage.reason: an image whose file name, alt text or class says it is the brand mark

elements.reason: the theme prints its own skip link

rules.doc: Framework-wide verdicts that settle an element before any scoring (lib/skeleton-rules.mjs holds the mechanisms; each verdict names its rule id on the row, and the review groups rows by it). Precedence: a client decision, then these rules, then a finaliser pick or a standing element decision, then the database scoring. Every block named here is checked against the framework database on load.

drawsChildren.reason: a block that draws the draft element's children itself, though it is neither a leaf nor holds an array item schema: the children are absorbed, never built

blocks.reason: reads its content from Site Info
draws its items, labels and carets from a WordPress menu
draws its items, numbers and carets from a WordPress menu

surfaceRoot.reason: a surface root whose kind names its block: a bar above the header is the header's top row, a menu panel is the mega panel, a drawer is the navigation drawer

entries.reason: a top bar above the header is the header's top row (sgs/site-header-row with its own hide-on-scroll setting), not a separate surface
a menu surface (the panel a navigation item opens) is sgs/mega-panel
a drawer surface is sgs/nav-drawer, whose own settings draw its top row, logo, close button and body

readingProgress.reason: a full-width bar a few pixels tall, fixed to the viewport, is the Floating UI reading progress setting, not a block
readingProgress.handover: Floating UI reading progress bar: its height and its colour or gradient (shared gradient picker) are site settings

decorationLayer.reason: a layer that holds nothing and only paints a fill, gradient or glow folds into the background of the block it sits in

decorativeShape.reason: a floating shape that draws an outline (a ring) is a decorative image

typedDivider.reason: a typed divider between items is the row's separators setting, not a block

homeLink.reason: the link around one or more logos (a mark and a wordmark) goes: the logo block links home itself

widthWrapper.reason: a centring width wrapper (max-width with auto margins) inside a header, footer, row or section block goes: that block sets its own width; its children take its place

listWrapper.reason: a bare wrapper whose only content is one list goes: the list block is that wrapper

backToTop.reason: a back-to-top control is a link whose source is 'top' (the shared link source): a container whose whole box is the link when it holds a label and an icon, a button when it is words alone

mapEmbed.reason: an embedded map is sgs/business-info's map display
mapEmbed.handover: map source: the Google Business Profile listing when Site Info has one (preferred), else the address

patterns: ^\s*(?:open now|closed now|open today|closed today|opens? at\b|closes? at\b|closed until\b)
openStatus.reason: a live open or closed line is sgs/business-info's open-status display, computed in the visitor's browser from the Site Info hours

hoursRows.reason: a day and its opening times laid out as a row is sgs/business-info's hours display (rows layout); the day and time columns are drawn by it

pillButton.reason: a link or button holding exactly one label (and a glyph) is one button whose glyph is its own icon; a toggle, a slider arrow and a link with no words are not pills; a lone link is a button too, which can be styled as a plain link

wholeCardLink.reason: a link holding two or more pieces of text, or a heading, is a container; its whole box is the link unless it ends in a call to action, which then holds the link (cardAction)

siteInfoLink.reason: a lone link to a phone number, an email address or a maps host is a button whose link reads Site Info (no typed tel: or mailto:), with its label from Site Info when the words are the value itself

linkSourceForKind.reason: the shared link source each Site Info kind becomes on a link

navigation.reason: the navigation inside a header is the menu bar block and inside a drawer the drawer menu block; both draw their items from a WordPress menu

solitaryIcon.reason: a glyph on its own (any icon library, an emoji alone, or a glyph the draft injects from a script value) is sgs/icon; an emoji inside running text stays typed in the text

label.reason: a short run of words set in capitals, wide tracking or a pill is a kicker, eyebrow or pill: sgs/label; never a control the visitor operates (a button, a click handler, a pressed or expanded state) and never a bare number

clientBuiltSurface.reason: a surface the client already built as a post (a header, drawer or mega menu) follows that post's block tree

logoElement.reason: a custom element named as a logo (its tag matches logoImage, such as <brand-logo>) is the logo block, which reads the site logo

columnHeading.reason: the first piece of text in a column that sits directly in a header or footer row heads that column (sgs/heading), whatever its type style

mediaElement.reason: a custom element the draft uses as an image placeholder (<image-slot>) is sgs/media

logoGrid.reason: a group of three or more links that each hold only an image (a logo wall) is sgs/gallery with a link per image; the links are its items

cardTitle.reason: the first plain piece of text in a whole-card link titles the card (sgs/heading); text set as a kicker stays a label

marquee.reason: a strip whose own animation loops a translate for ever (the motion inventory's record, never a name) is a marquee: logos make sgs/brand-strip, labels make sgs/trust-bar, and the repeated items are its items; the route writes no marquee motion until M7

trustBar.reason: a trust bar is a section block (block_composition.container_kind section): a page's own section that is a row of short non-interactive labels side by side, each with at most a glyph, at least one naming a capability the framework database records for sgs/trust-bar (accreditation, certification, halal), is sgs/trust-bar with the labels as its items; the same badges inside a section are sgs/label blocks in a row (Bean, 2026-10-13). The ignored capabilities (collection, features, icons) describe the block, not what its badges say

hero.reason: the first section of a page holding its h1 is sgs/hero (its label, heading, text and buttons are its content; an image inside makes it the split hero)

heroInner.reason: inside a hero, its image is the hero's own split media and its layout wrappers go (the hero lays out its content and media columns); a wrapper laying items side by side (a button group, a row of labels) stays

marqueeFrame.reason: the frame that only clips or fades a marquee track goes: sgs/brand-strip draws its own overflow, and a masked edge fade belongs to its marquee motion (Bean, 2026-10-13)

alignWrapper.reason: a wrapper whose only declared styles align or space its content (text alignment, padding, margin) goes: the blocks around and inside it align and pad themselves; anything that paints, positions or lays out stays (Bean, 2026-10-13)

cardAction.reason: a card link that ends in a short call to action (a glyph beside it, or below two other pieces of text) is a plain card, and the call to action is the button that holds the link (Bean, 2026-10-13: the card is not a link; the button is the link)

formControl.reason: a form control is the SGS field block for its rendered type (a lone required checkbox is the consent field); a <label> wrapped round it goes (Bean, 2026-10-19)
formControl.fieldTextReason: the field's label, required marker, hint or character count: the field block's own label, required and help text settings draw it (Bean, 2026-10-19)

cardHeading.reason: the first piece of text in a card that is not a bare number, set bold and larger than the text after it, titles the card (sgs/heading), whether or not the card is a link (Bean, 2026-10-19)

dotMarker.reason: a small dot or short bar beside text is the marker of the block holding the text (a label's dot, a list item's marker, the separator between a row's items); stacked rows of a marker and one piece of text are one list (Bean, 2026-10-19)
